summary: Almotriptan is an oral triptan for acute treatment of migraine attacks (with or without aura) in adults and adolescents 12-17 years. It is a selective 5-HT1B/1D agonist that causes cranial vasoconstriction and inhibits release of vasoactive neuropeptides. It is contraindicated in ischemic heart, cerebrovascular, and peripheral vascular disease, uncontrolled hypertension, and within 24 hours of ergots or another triptan. It is for acute treatment only, not prophylaxis.
indications: Acute treatment of migraine attacks (with or without aura) in adults
Acute treatment of migraine headache pain in adolescents 12-17 years with attacks usually lasting >=4 hours

moa: Almotriptan binds with high affinity to 5-HT1B and 5-HT1D receptors. Agonism at 5-HT1B receptors causes constriction of dilated intracranial extracerebral blood vessels, while 5-HT1D agonism inhibits release of pro-inflammatory vasoactive neuropeptides and reduces transmission in the trigeminal pain pathway. These actions relieve the vasodilation and neurogenic inflammation thought to underlie migraine.

absolute: Ischemic coronary artery disease, coronary vasospasm (including Prinzmetal angina), or other significant cardiovascular disease
History of stroke or transient ischemic attack (cerebrovascular syndromes)
Peripheral vascular disease including ischemic bowel disease
Use within 24 hours of an ergotamine/ergot-type drug or another 5-HT1 agonist (triptan)
relative: Cardiovascular risk factors (assess before use; first dose under supervision)
Hepatic or severe renal impairment (reduce dose)
monitor: Cardiovascular evaluation in patients with risk factors

preg: There are limited human data. Use almotriptan during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known to what extent almotriptan is excreted in human milk; exercise caution when administering to a nursing woman.
renal: In patients with severe renal impairment, the recommended starting dose is 6.25 mg and the maximum daily dose should not exceed 12.5 mg.
hepatic: In patients with hepatic impairment, the recommended starting dose is 6.25 mg and the maximum daily dose should not exceed 12.5 mg.

major: Ergot-containing/ergot-type medications (additive vasospasm - separate by 24 hours)
Other 5-HT1 agonists / triptans (additive vasospastic effects - separate by 24 hours)
moderate: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir - may raise almotriptan levels)
interactions.alcohol: No direct pharmacologic interaction; alcohol can independently trigger migraine

serious: Myocardial ischemia / infarction and serious arrhythmias

counsel: Take at the first sign of a migraine for best effect
Do not take more than 25 mg in one day or treat more than about 4 attacks per month without advice
Do not use within 24 hours of another triptan or an ergot medicine
Stop and seek care for chest pain, pressure, or tightness, or signs of stroke
Tell your doctor about heart disease, high blood pressure, and antidepressants
Frequent use can cause rebound (medication-overuse) headaches
pk: Headache relief often begins within 30 minutes to 2 hours
Peak plasma concentration about 1-3 hours after dosing
Action sufficient for a single attack; second dose allowed after 2 hours
Store at controlled room temperature 20-25 C
pearls: Among the better-tolerated triptans, with a relatively low rate of chest symptoms
Bioavailability about 70% and unaffected by food
A second dose helps recurrence but does not rescue a non-responding first dose
Use only after a clear migraine diagnosis; it is not for prophylaxis or cluster headache
Limit treatment days to reduce medication-overuse headache
missed: Almotriptan is taken only as needed for an acute migraine, so there is no regular schedule and no missed dose. Take it when a migraine starts, observing the 2-hour gap before any repeat dose and the 25 mg daily maximum.
overdose: There is limited experience with overdose. Doses up to 150 mg were administered without serious adverse events in some volunteers, but vasospastic effects are possible. Provide supportive care and monitor for at least 12 hours or while symptoms persist; the effect of dialysis on clearance is unknown.
